Sofia: FYI I ran the long-seq perf sweep on SM90 + Triton for the paged/fused attention variants. Seeing a consistent latency regression (~5-8%) vs SM80 for the paged-Triton path when KV density is low. attaching quick numbers below.

build-bot: perf-ci: 1829991200 -> regression detected: p99 +6.3% (paged-attn, Triton, sm90, seq=4k, batch=2) :eyes:

Raghu: Can you paste the microprof? is it kernel launch overhead or memory-bound?

Sofia: microprof snippet:```
GPU: A100-SM90
Model: gpt-7b sharded
seq_len: 4096, batch:2
KV density: 12% (sparse prefixes mostly)
Triton paged-attn kernel time: 42.3ms
CUDA fused kernel (fallback): 39.1ms
L2 writeback stall increased ~18% on sm90 kernels
```

Oliver: Interesting — on SM90 we see L2 behaviour change with new cache paths. Triton-generated kernels are emitting more vectorized stores on the page-scan loop. That increases eviction churn for small KV caches. If KV density < 20% and sequence > 2048 we should prefer the CUDA fused kernel.

Elaine: Agreed. Proposed selection heuristic:```json
{"selection_order": ["fused_cuda","triton_paged","flash_variant"],"rules": [{"if": "seq>2048 && kv_density<0.2","use": "fused_cuda"},{"if": "seq<=2048 && batch>=4","use": "triton_paged"},{"fallback": "flash_variant"} ] }
```

Raghu: Quick question on measurement: how are you computing kv_density? we need a consistent metric across hosted/dedicated.

Sofia: kv_density = total_cached_tokens / (total_keys_emitted_by_model). For the sweep I sampled over 1k requests from the generation trace and averaged. In practice we can use per-route rolling stat exported to the console.

Oliver: Also noticed Triton kernels on CUDA 12.3 emit different SASS for ldg/stg vs 12.1. Might explain the L2 stalls. We should gate triton_paged availability by (cuda_version >= 12.2 && driver >= 535). Otherwise force fused_cuda.

build-bot: perf-ci: rerun scheduled by @Elaine for 1829993000 (cuda 12.1 vs 12.3 matrix)

Elaine: I'll run the matrix tonight. Plan: (sm80, sm90) x (cuda 12.1,12.3) x (triton latest, triton-compat). Will record: p50/p95/p99, mem BW, l2_stalls, kernel_invocations.

Raghu: If tests confirm, we'll add an explicit kernel capability probe at startup: run a tiny attention shape (seq=512,batch=1,kv_sparsity=0.1) and measure L2 stall ratio; if > threshold disable triton_paged for that node. Cheap probe (~10ms).

Sofia: One more real-world note: some customer workloads with long prompts + short continuations show high prefix reuse -> higher kv_density. In those cases triton_paged is still best on SM90. So selection must be workload-aware, not purely arch-based.

Oliver: Agreed. We'll implement a multi-factor score: score = alpha*kv_density - beta*L2_stall_est - gamma*(seq_norm) + delta*(batch_scale). Choose kernel with highest score. Start with simple rules (Elaine JSON) then iterate.

Elaine: I'll add a draft PR to runtime/kernel-selector with the rule engine + config toggles. tagging @Raghu for review.

Sofia: Thanks. If PR lands before tomorrow's deploy window, we'll flip the fallback and run canary on dedicated pool A.

Raghu: Sounds good. keep the canary small (5% traffic) and monitor p99 and generation costs. Also log chosen kernel per-request (anonymized) for analysis.

build-bot: note: perf-alerts configured for 5% regressions on p99 for canary.
